permission_boundary: Only get_mempolicy executed successfully. set_mempolicy symbol exists but permission/semantics were not tested because policy modification was prohibited.

official_sources.finding: Explicit node allocation adds __GFP_THISNODE; high-order host allocations use __GFP_COMP.
nv_alloc_contig_pages chooses NV_ALLOC_PAGES_NODE(order) or NV_GET_FREE_PAGES(order); zero allocation returns NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY. This is host physical-page allocation, not GPU VRAM accounting.
NV_ALLOC_PAGES_NODE maps to alloc_pages_node(nid,gfp_mask,order); NV_GET_FREE_PAGES maps to __get_free_pages.
EnableUserNUMAManagement concerns onlining/offlining device memory as NUMA on certain POWER9 platforms. Not evidence of host-memory policy on this x86 H100 PCIe.
Policy is per calling thread, inherited by newly created fork/clone threads and preserved over exec; applies to new page allocations, not migration of prior pages.

callchain_boundary: Public kernel source supports a plausible host-allocation failure mechanism, but proprietary userspace libcuda cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain internals and this incident ioctl-to-kernel allocation call chain are not established. No root-cause attribution.

before_arm: Use an owned new scalar diagnostic child, fixed UUID and unchanged RLIMIT/CPU affinity. Hold shared benchmark lock and record contemporaneous driver/GPU/NUMA state.
Before CUDA import/init or new library threads, save caller get_mempolicy(mode including flags,nodemask,maxnode) and errno; save CPU affinity; reject bind if node not in Mems_allowed_list.
Call set_mempolicy(MPOL_BIND=2,one-node mask,maxnode adequate), record return/errno and read back. Do not use modern flags absent on kernel3.10.
arm: Only context initialization/retain/current/priority query/sync explicitly chosen by root; no MRI/large tensor. Record each raw driver code and ioctl/host allocation outcomes.
No existing-context destruction: only release contexts/retains created and owned by this new child.
finally_restore: In the SAME creator thread, release each successful own primary-context retain exactly once, clear current own context if applicable, then restore saved mode/nodemask.
For saved MPOL_DEFAULT=0, restore with set_mempolicy(0,NULL,0), not a zero non-NULL nodemask. For saved nondefault, restore original flags/mask/maxnode.

Read get_mempolicy back and compare original; log any restore failure clearly. Restore affinity if experiment changed it, though memory-only arm should keep affinity constant. Exit owned child after each arm.
thread_and_order_limits: Restoring creator thread does not restore already-created helper threads, which inherited the temporary policy. Existing helper threads before bind also do not retroactively change policy.

Same-process node0->node1 primary context release/retain may retain driver caches/helper threads; reverse order repeats alone cannot erase that history. Use same-thread bind/restore to validate restoration, but use matched fresh child per arm with randomized order for causal node comparison.
Explicit alloc_pages_node(nid,__GFP_THISNODE,order) driver allocations may bypass userspace default policy. A no-effect bind result does not rule out driver GPU-local host-page failure.
performance_risk: Node1 may place host buffers remotely to GPU0 NUMA0, changing transfer latency and CPU memory access. Binding may restrict fallback and provoke allocation failure; diagnosis only, not production fix.

Previously allocated pages are not moved by set_mempolicy; restoring policy does not migrate pages created while bound. Context-only results do not establish whole-pipeline numerical/performance equivalence.
